Ned Lamont

Democratic / Working Families candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Connecticut · Incumbent

Governor of Connecticut; former telecommunications business owner

Ned Lamont is the Democratic governor of Connecticut. He took office in 2019 and won reelection in 2022. He is running for a third term in 2026 with Lt. Gov. Susan Bysiewicz as his running mate, after facing state Rep. Josh Elliott in the August Democratic primary.

Where Lamont stands

Affordability / cost of living
Lists affordability as a main priority on his campaign website.
Early childhood education
Proposes putting universal pre-K in place statewide.
Health care costs
Proposes lowering health insurance premiums for middle- and low-income families. Cites capping insulin costs at $25 per month as one of his accomplishments.
Environment / open space
Proposes permanently preserving 21% of the state as open space.
Higher education
Cites creating debt-free community college for Connecticut residents as one of his accomplishments.
Technology / online safety
Signed legislation in June 2026 that set up youth online safety protections, described as new AI regulations.

Background

  • Governor of Connecticut, 2019–present (elected 2018, reelected 2022)
  • Founder and owner of a telecommunications business
  • 2026 Democratic nominee for governor, also on the Working Families line; running mate Susan Bysiewicz

Also running for Governor and Lieutenant Governor

  • Ryan Fazio Republican / Independent
